_disclaimer: All records below are either (a) well-established public-knowledge reference alleles used purely as teaching examples, never real patient data, or (b) explicitly synthetic fixtures invented to illustrate a documented statistical pattern from the cited literature (see README.md > Data and citations). None of this file represents a real patient, a real ClinVar accession number, or real-world diagnostic performance.

variants.label: public-reference
variants.note: The well-known public-domain beta-globin missense variant that causes sickle haemoglobin (HbS); used here only as a canonical, pedagogically-clear example of a pathogenic call feeding into a real approved therapy (see therapy_table.json).

variants.label: synthetic-illustrative
variants.note: Fully synthetic fixture. Modeled on the 'clinically substantial conflict' pattern reported in Oliver et al. 2020 (epilepsy genes in ClinVar, ~3.2% of shared variants crossed the Uncertain-Significance / Likely-Pathogenic line). Invented to demo the Conflict and Compliance agents reacting to a threshold-crossing disagreement -- not a real gene finding.

variants.label: synthetic-illustrative
variants.note: Fully synthetic fixture demonstrating the BA1 'too common to be pathogenic' stand-alone benign rule -- shows the ACMG agent is a real branching rule engine, not a pathogenic-only demo.
